composition: Nominal composition Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–0.5Be (wt%); Fe is the balance. The alloy was melted from high-purity elements — Fe, Mn, Al, C and Be, each 99.99%. The base Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C matrix supplies Mn and C as austenite-stabilising elements (for ductility) and Al as the main density-reducing element; 0.5 wt% Be is added on top of this base to attempt further density reduction and to introduce Be–Fe compound precipitation. By atomic size, Be (111 pm) is smaller than Fe (124 pm) and dissolves substitutionally, whereas C (77 pm) dissolves interstitially and Al (143 pm) is oversized relative to Fe. In this as-cast steel the atomic concentration ratio of Fe atoms to Be atoms is 18.7:1.
summary: As-cast Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–0.5Be (wt%) low-density steel, prepared by vacuum induction melting and ingot casting and left in the terminal as-cast condition (no heat treatment, no thermal deformation). It is one member of a Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe (x = 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5 wt%) series in which beryllium (ρ = 1.848 g/cm³) is added as a lightweight alloying element to further lower the density and to explore its effect on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the Fe–Mn–Al–C system. The core question addressed with this sample is how 0.5 wt% Be partitions between solid solution and Be–Fe compounds in the as-solidified structure, and whether it already promotes ferrite formation.
